page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on KVM virtualization. It features 2 vCPUs allocated across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 16 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not bundled, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent disk access. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations reflect entry-level compute capability alongside modest memory subsystem speeds. In stress-ng evaluations, the server produced scores of 1097.18 on single-core tests and 1457.68 on multi-core tests. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 924.0 and a multi-core score of 1093.0, with clang software compilation reaching 1441.0. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 10.06 GB/s, while write bandwidth measured 9.35 GB/s. Application tests showed static web serving throughput of 1.25 GB/s and Redis performance measuring 1.51 million SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high memory density relative to core allocation, enabling workloads requiring substantial RAM without requiring extra CPU licensing or resource overhead. The principal tradeoff is restrained computational throughput, which makes it less viable for compute-heavy parallel processing. Workload fit encompasses lightweight in-memory caching, low-traffic database deployments, staging systems, and background batch jobs requiring moderate RAM buffers.
